key_insight: A triadic LLM–teacher–student workflow can improve K-12 writing at scale when the LLM generates ideas and the teacher filters and contextualizes feedback.
engineering_relevance: This paper shows that practical educational AI systems should use role-specialized human-AI collaboration rather than fully automated feedback, especially in high-stakes K-12 settings.
method: Built a triadic collaboration system for K-12 writing support
Used a multidimensional evaluation framework grounded in Systemic Functional Linguistics
Traced suggestion trajectories to measure how LLM and teacher feedback affect writing development
evidence_signal: The study analyzes 57,954 essays from 10,195 students across 120 schools over two years, providing large-scale empirical evidence of writing improvement.
watch_item: The reported ceiling effect suggests that more linguistic expansion from the LLM can eventually provide diminishing returns, so feedback must adapt to student proficiency.
paper_title: Double-Edged Sword or Sharp Tool? Designing and Evaluating Triadic LLM-Teacher Collaboration for K-12 Writing at Scale
